claims.text: The retained Colliers excerpt advertises abstraction quality-control measures and annual expense reconciliations; it does not establish measured accuracy or recovery outcomes.

The retained MRI Ireland excerpt says its lease administration serves occupiers only and mentions monthly reconciliation. This is an international operating-model analogue, not US market-size evidence.
The retained Mohr excerpt advertises per-location, per-transaction, resource-based and performance-driven pricing and senior review of AI-generated findings; no measured savings are retained.
The retained Savills UK excerpt advertises recurring portfolio/database maintenance and monthly reporting. It does not establish US revenues or renewal quality.
The retained LORICO excerpt lists rent/common-area collections, payment-obligation enforcement and date calendars. Buyer ownership and contractual risk allocation are not established by these lines.
The retained IREM course excerpt names commercial lease administration and its effect on workload; it does not establish mandatory credentials or workforce availability.

The retained CoreNet excerpt only lists lease management administration alongside location intelligence and facilities management. The extract alone does not establish AI adoption or measured productivity.

The retained Hughes Marino excerpt advertises date monitoring, charge validation and monthly reporting; it does not independently establish market size, acquisition availability, or operating performance.

The advertised recurring record updates, dates, charge validation and reporting suggest a desk-based administrative workflow worth testing as an operating-market boundary. This does not establish that NAICS531390 owns that market, or replace exclusions in the official source.
These retained excerpts do not establish US demand magnitude, acquisition supply, company values, margins, labor representation or eligibility. No eligibility exception or target status is supplied.

The retained LORICO lines advertise rent collections, common-area collections, payment-obligation enforcement and date calendars, but do not identify the contracting buyer, payer/payee roles, custody of client funds, or contractual risk allocation. They do not establish whether these activities belong inside the proposed occupier-side workflow, a landlord-side service, another operating boundary, or multiple boundaries. Inclusion and exclusion remain research questions; do not transfer a buyer identified in another provider excerpt to these activities without supporting evidence.

gaps.question: Do recurring occupier-side lease administration services constitute a distinct operating market related to this family, or should they be mapped elsewhere, left unresolved or rejected? No family membership is asserted by this research attachment.
What US demand, customer retention, margins, workforce/labor exposure, independent acquisition population, EV and deal-price evidence supports this proposed service boundary?
Re-verify retained excerpts against source pages where fuller context is necessary; original HTML bodies were not retained, and checksums establish frozen excerpt bytes only.

For rent/common-area collections and payment-obligation work described in the retained LORICO excerpt, who contracts for the service, who owes or receives the payment, and what custody, authorization and contractual obligations does the provider assume? Determine whether each activity belongs within an occupier-side lease-administration boundary, another boundary, overlapping offerings, or remains unresolved. Advertising an activity does not establish its buyer-specific operating scope; neither inclusion nor exclusion is prescribed.
